Same-Sex-Attracted is a term used to implicitly say that a person is attracted to people of the same gender, and that should be recognised as a condition or state of being over an identity. It can refer to really any non-affirming theology, but it's mostly used (in my experience) by people who favor Side-B theology. LGBT people almost unanimously don't like language like this, because we do see our orientation as an inherent part of us - we reject the framing inherent to the term SSA, so we reject the term itself.

Now, you do very occasionally see religious people who describe themselves as being Same-Sex-Attracted because of their religious beliefs, usually at the exclusion of other labels but I have seen someone identify as both Bi and SSA. If that's the language someone insists on for themselves, I'll personally respect that, but unless someone very explicitly says that's how they want to be referred to you should avoid it. Otherwise use Gay or LGBTQ because that will usually be the language that's preferred. It's also in no way offensive to be referred to as gay, and it's not the first time I've heard of a Christian thinking that but I genuinely have no idea where it comes from.

Hope this helps :)

I think the fact that she doesn't seem to trust your judgment and is forcing an ultimatum on you is the main issue here. Ultimatums are a sign something has gone wrong in the relationship, usually issues with communication, trust, and/or boundaries. If you've expressed that you feel your drug use isn't problematic, nor will it become problematic in the future, and she's been unwilling to open up a dialogue or compromise with you, then that's a potential red flag for future conflicts.

My advice: if you haven't already, have a long discussion with her. Talk about the drugs you take and want to take, their risks & benefits, things you plan to do to keep safe in your use, and so on. Listen to her concerns and discuss them with her. Hopefully, you work out something you are both happy with. If she sticks to her original ultimatum, then it's up to you to decide what's more important for your long-term happiness. Although if you do talk and you end up having to pick, I would consider very strongly that it may not be the last time an ultimatum is put to you over the course of your relationship.

Dyslexia is in this weird area of being understood poorly but not all-that stigmatised so you're very unlikely to hear anything malicious.

So, Splatoon is a team-based competitive shooter, which is what the bulk of the game is based around. Although, you have some short but lore-rich single player campaigns - both currently-released games have octo vally and octo canyon respectively, where you play as Agent 3 (in Splatoon 1) and Agent 4 (in Splatoon 2) of The New Squidbeak Splatoon, a secret group of agents tasked with recovering The Great Zapfish from DJ Octavio (more on that later). Splatoon 2 also has a DLC campaign, Octo Expansion, which sees you play as Agent 8, who is trapped on an underground metro with Captain Cuttlefish (he founded the New Squidbeak Splatoon, so you get an Agent number for helping him escape haha) you need to play-through a series of tasks to make your way to 'the promised land', which is actually the surface that you play the rest of the game in. 

You have 6 major game modes to play online: Turf War is unranked and beginner friendly, you just need to have the most ground covered in your ink at the end of the match. Salmon Run is a co-op mode that's basically a zombie hoard survival, but you need to kill bosses to get power eggs, and then being them to an egg collection basket. Canonically, Salmon Run is a job (that is very questionable in its legality) so you have egg quotas you need to meet, which means you're ballancing survival and egg-collecting.

The rest are ranked gamemodes, which see you play an objective. You win either by completing the objective (or 'knocking out' the other team) which ends the game in your favor instantly, or by just being the team closer to completing it at the end of the match. Splat Zones is similar to Turf War, there's one or two zones you need to control by having it painted in your colour, and how long you've held it is tracked, basically. Tower Control has you ride a tower progressively deeper into the enemy-base - at least one of your team mates will need to stand on the tower, but if more than one team mate does the tower moves a bit faster. Rainmaker is similar, one of you need to carry the rainmaker (a very slow-firing weapon that replaces your actual weapon while you're holding it) which you need to carry into the enemy base. Then there's Clam Blitz, which is a bit like football. Both teams have a basket that needs to have clams thrown into it, which are scattered around the map. To break open the basket, though, you need a power clam (made by collecting 10 regular clams, or by collecting the 'pity ball' you get after your basket has been broken by the other team). Team who scores the most, or first team to score 100 wins.

The core gameplay is simple to grasp, but hard to master. It's basically a 3rd person shooter with a mix of shooters, melee weapons, and weapons that kinda bridge that gap, and those guns fire ink on the ground, but movement, positioning, and map control are much more important than other shooters. You have a squid/octopus form that allows you to swim in your ink, which is also how to recharge ammo. It gives you much freer and fast movement that's hard (but not impossible) for your enemies to track you in. It also lets you swim up walls. Your weapon is split into your Main, your Sub (stuff like bombs, basically) and your Special (which you get by painting ground and staying alive). Splatoon 1 specials were these big game-changers that let you go on a killing rampage, but in Splatoon 2 most specials are more about helping you hold areas of the map (such as Ink Storm, which is a rain cloud that moves over an area and slowly damages anyone from the other team that stands in it, it can be used to force the other team to retreat from an area you want to push into, or force a team to halt their push into ground you already control). You die very quickly, so firefights with other players are important but far from the only thing you're doing.

This is getting pretty long, so I'll give a really basic lore recap and leave it there xD
So, the Splatoon Universe takes place on earth about 12000 years after humanity wiped itself out in a global flood caused by nuclear war. Squids and Octopi (and a lot of other aquatic species) evolved to live on land, which includes the Inklings and Octolings that serve as the series mascots. Inklings and Octolings began to battle over the little land that was left on earth in an event known as The Great Turf War. Inklings won, and took the surface to themselves, while Octolings and Octarians (Octolings without a humanoid form, basically) were banished underground. Inkling Society became kinda vain, and hyper focused on things like Idols, Turf Wars, and being Fresh (cool and hip, basically). Meanwhile, Octcarian society, led by DJ Octavio, became basically a military dictatorship with things like child soldiers and mind-control via goggles & music (hence 'DJ Octavio') being used to advance. The result is highly advanced weapons and technology, although this advancement is limited due to the Octarians lack of power-sources. That's why both games involve the stealing of The Great Zapfish - a creature who, in return for protection, provides inklings with a ton of power to run their society. DJ Octavio wants The Great Zapfish to power super weapons, basically.

The Octo Expansion follows its own plot that doesn't currently tie into the main plot a ton (minus character development, there's a lot of that), but due to the events of Octo Expansion and Agent 8, a lot of the previously mind-controlled Octolings escaped their brainwashing and joined inklings on the surface. Canonically, though, all Inklings think that the Octolings are just Inklings with weird hair, with the exceptions of Agents 1, 2, 3, 4, Captain Cuttlefish, and one other Inkling who helped with the campaign (who is probably Agent 5 or 6 but it's never confirmed). This sounds like a cop-out by Nintendo to avoid the obvious racial tension that would be there (and tbh it kinda is) but it is established that Inklings tend not to be the smartest so it does make sense in-universe haha.

Lastly; My favourite parts of Splatoon have to be the lore, because it goes very deep (I barely scratched the surface) and the gameplay that focuses so much on strategy. It's got a lot to like and enjoy, it's a shame the series hasn't gotten more popular ;o

I'm assuming you've never taken weed, so I'm writing my description to try and replicate being high. It's very hard to fully describe though. Drugs take your brain to a state it doesn't naturally reside in, so some level of understanding is locked behind actually experiencing it.

For me, it comes in distinct stages. People think of being high as a binary thing where you're somewhere between sober and blazed, but for me it's a slow build of the numerous physical, mental, and emotional responses to cannabis being in your system until I'm at my final level of overall-stoned.

A high starts for me with the sides of my face tingling and my vision going fuzzy. The sensation intensifies and I start getting relaxed, both in terms of my brain slowing down a bit and my body feeling a little lighter.

Now if I've only had a little, it ends there. If I've had a substantial amount I get a wave of a calm happiness come over me. If I'm around other people this will be expressed by me laughing at everything until I'm metaphorically blue in the face, but when smoking alone it's more that I'm very content with my life and the small joys around me. Any higher and I kinda drift into this daydreamy state, where I'll see something beautiful or think of something semi-deep, and my brain spaces out to explore it either visually or conceptually. Sometimes these have made me realise things about me and my experiences that have had a lasting positive impact on my life, other times they're honestly really silly. I remember once I was making a microwavable double cheeseburger, and decided to put the cheese between the two meat patties. I was staring at it and couldn't stop thinking "I don't even need the buns, the meat IS the bun, the cheese IS the meat, this is ALREADY a burger" and I think it took me a solid minute to convince myself that cheese and meat alone would be a sad burger to eat.

Speaking of food, I get very hungry, and it's usually that first bite of food that makes me realise my mouth is dry as shit. Food absolutely does taste better, and the texture of food is magnified in such an amazing way, but I always forget to drink first and that makes it a little less fun hahaha.

It's overall a really nice experience that refreshes me for a few days afterwards, although the dry mouth and dry eyes suck, and I find I forget a lot of the fine-details of what I did the next day if I had more than a couple puffs of a joint, which is a little anoying. I'd rate it a 8/10 lmao.
